quote.text: A man with a watch knows what time it is. A man with two watches is never sure.
quote.author: Known as Segal’s law; the attribution has never been traced to a source, and the line is best treated as an anonymous mid-twentieth-century proverb

stories.headline: The damage is a mould line, and the comb without one is £4.50
stories.dek: Cut the comb from a sheet instead of moulding it and the ridge cannot exist. The rest of this desk is what the other objects cost.

stories.headline: They call themselves Neanderthals, and most of them own a machine
stories.dek: A craft where the entry ritual is a single translucent shaving, the central scientific document is a Japanese microscope video from 1994, and the honest reason people do it has nothing to do with the furniture.

stories.headline: Four flights a day to Saigon, and twenty-six fewer flat beds
stories.dek: Singapore Airlines rebuilt its Vietnam winter on Wednesday. Frequencies to Ho Chi Minh City rise a third; total capacity falls three per cent and Business falls fourteen. Da Nang is the unambiguous win.

stories.kicker: The World · The Gulf, week four
stories.headline: Europe’s October is zero. The oil price fell anyway
stories.dek: Aramco has told its European term customers there will be no Saudi crude for them next month. In the same week it sold sixty million barrels out of Ras Tanura — east, through the strait everyone calls closed.

stories.headline: Two numbers, both correct, and only one of them is about tonight
stories.dek: The island’s twenty-four-hour index read 108 at six o’clock on Saturday evening. The hourly reading at the same moment was 61. The agency publishes both on purpose, and tells you which one to use.

stories.kicker: Technology · The agent in your repository
stories.headline: Seven hundred megabytes, and you hold none of the keys
stories.dek: A developer noticed a cache folder had grown past 700MB. It turned out to be his entire git history, encrypted with a public key served fresh by the vendor, uploaded before every prompt — and the private key never leaves the cloud.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The pocket that does not buzz
stories.headline: The price everyone printed is the Hong Kong price
stories.dek: Onyx’s new pocket E Ink Android takes a pen, wears aluminium and costs US$339.99. Every review this week said US$319.99 — which is the figure on the Asia listing, twenty dollars below the American one.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The watch you cannot buy
stories.headline: It is called Perpetual and it is not a perpetual calendar
stories.dek: Two hundred hours of patent work to make an annual calendar from two extra components, a moon cut from meteorite — and no product page, no Singapore price, and a reviewer who says out loud who gets one.

stories.headline: Ninety-five from the critics, ninety-one from the crowd — and a record nobody expected a video game to hold
stories.dek: Two weeks ago this desk had a film at thirty-five per cent from critics and ninety-two from the audience. This week the numbers changed sides, and the film that did it opened in Singapore a day before America saw it.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Fifty per cent of what, exactly
stories.headline: A press release said “fifty per cent more effective.” For most children the trial found nothing at all
stories.dek: A 1,793-child randomised trial across forty-four German schools, mean age thirteen point one, tested therapy against media literacy. The headline belongs to 205 children. The other 1,588 are the story.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The week the average said nothing
stories.headline: Global bonds finished flat, and that flat number hid two opposite weeks
stories.dek: Treasuries sold off, JGBs rallied on a Bank of Japan hike, and the global-aggregate wrapper netted to zero — no cushion and no second wound. Meanwhile the Fed deleted the word the market used as a stopping rule.

stories.kicker: Fitness · The trial and the correction, a fortnight apart
stories.headline: Three months of exercise missed its primary outcome. Two weeks earlier, the literature behind it was corrected
stories.dek: Fifty-two people aged forty-five to sixty-five, three sessions a week for twelve weeks. Mood moved. Cognition did not. And the stem-cell result came out with the wrong sign.

stories.headline: Sumo went on sale yesterday morning, and the one hard deadline on this page is ten days away
stories.dek: Every row below was re-checked against a promoter, a venue or an official ticketing page before it was printed. One price set belongs to a different year, and one museum closes in eleven days for nineteen months.

stories.headline: Forty-eight of them carried it back up the mountain
stories.dek: Bhutan built the best-designed wild-harvest market in the Himalaya: open auctions, published prices, policed permits. This summer the auctions stopped clearing. In the customs file underneath, the country had shipped thirty-nine per cent more of the stuff for fifteen per cent less money.
